en.title: After Accelerationism: Artificial Intelligence, Labour Income and the Struggle over the Pace of the Twenty-First Century
en.deck: Why accelerating AI capability does not automatically produce broad prosperity: employment, early-career opportunity, capital ownership, basic income, electrical infrastructure, governance and autonomous warfare under 2026 evidence.
en.regime: Fast technical diffusion, contested labour effects and unequal infrastructures.
en.key_risk: Mistaking task exposure for unemployment, announced capital expenditure for delivered productivity and corporate statements for verified policy outcomes.
watch: Youth hiring and employment in exposed occupations
Cost per verified task and measured firm-level productivity
Worker income share and cloud/chip concentration
en.search_text: After Accelerationism: AI, labour income and the pace of technological progress, basic income, early-career employment, governance and security

pt-BR.title: Depois do aceleracionismo: inteligência artificial, renda do trabalho e a disputa pelo ritmo do século XXI
pt-BR.deck: Por que a rápida expansão da capacidade de IA não produz automaticamente prosperidade compartilhada: emprego, entrada na carreira, propriedade do capital, renda básica, infraestrutura elétrica, governança e guerra autônoma à luz de evidências de 2026.
pt-BR.regime: Difusão técnica rápida, impactos laborais contestados e infraestrutura desigual.
pt-BR.key_risk: Confundir exposição de tarefas com desemprego, investimento anunciado com produtividade entregue e declarações empresariais com resultados políticos comprovados.
watch: Contratações de jovens e emprego em ocupações expostas
Custo por tarefa validada e produtividade empresarial medida
Participação salarial e concentração em chips/nuvem
Conexão elétrica de centros de dados e demanda
Evidências independentes sobre segurança de IA e armas autônomas
pt-BR.search_text: Depois do aceleracionismo: inteligência artificial, renda do trabalho, renda básica, contratação de iniciantes, governança e segurança

producer_checks.information_cutoff: 2 November 2026, America/Sao_Paulo; cites explicitly dated 2024, 2025 and 2026 sources and keeps observation years separate from publication dates.
producer_checks.research_depth: English 5,584 approximate words, PT-BR 6,064 approximate words; 15 substantive H2 sections per locale. Both manuscripts provide methodological distinctions and competing scenarios.
producer_checks.source_check: 16 distinct URLs per locale including Stanford HAI, ILO, IMF, Anthropic, IEA, NBER, NATO, United Nations, OpenAI, Dario Amodei and IBGE; principal numerical series checked against source presentations.
producer_checks.translation_parity: Matching three numeric chart series, equivalent article outline, tables, key claims, qualifications and source list in English and Brazilian Portuguese.
producer_checks.visual_signature: Three quantitative charts each locale: survey AI adoption 55/88%, IMF exposure 60/40/26%, IEA data-centre electricity 415/945 TWh. Four analytical tables, one causal flow and one regional comparison map per locale, with numeric values identical.
producer_checks.methodology: Separate task exposure from unemployment, survey adoption from deployment, scenario from observation, corporate statements from implementation, controlled research from political endorsement; contrast 3-4 conditional paths and note falsifiers.
producer_checks.draft_status: Bilingual staging completed. Pending v2 is submitted for independent fact-check, editorial depth and visual QA; producer does not approve its own research.
limitations: Source-page URLs were reviewed against published institutional summaries, but independent line-by-line verification and online availability remain QA responsibilities.
No original causal estimate of AI-induced labour displacement or fiscal UBI model is claimed.
Comparative geography table states mechanisms, not an audited country ranking.

revision_reason: First current-affairs systems study under the new accelerationism editorial line; complements the October intellectual-history and technofeudalism publications.
